definition: genus name.
rule: As printed in the paper. Name letters only: remove marks printed with the name (e.g. '?', '(*?)', '*'); write the printed form in notes, e.g. "name printed as '?stenophylla'".

definition: species epithet.
rule: As printed in the paper. Epithet only; infraspecific rank and name (subsp., var., f.) go in subsp. Name letters only: remove marks printed with the name (e.g. '?', '(*?)', '*'); write the printed form in notes, e.g. "name printed as '?stenophylla'". Hyphenated epithet is one word, no spaces ('novae- zelandiae' -> 'novae-zelandiae').

definition: Infraspecific taxon: rank abbreviation + name (subspecies, variety or form).
rule: Keep the rank word, written as subsp., var. or f. ('ssp.' or 'subsp' -> 'subsp.'; 'variety' -> 'var.'; 'forma' -> 'f.'); other ranks (e.g. nothosubsp.) as printed. Remove other marks printed with the name (e.g. '?'); printed form in notes. Never '*'; native or introduced status goes in native_status.
example: subsp. buxifolia | var. lanceolatus | f. glauca

definition: Full species name.
rule: genus + ' ' + species. Never include the subspecies, variety or form, or '*'.

allowed_values: native | introduced | exotic | naturalised | weed | as printed
definition: Whether the taxon is native or not native to the study location, in the paper's own words. The reference region (e.g. NSW, Australia) is whatever the paper uses.
rule: Use the paper's term, in lower case: from a symbol or code defined in the paper (e.g. '*' = introduced; code 'Exotic'), a table column, or the text. Unmarked taxon -> 'native' only if the paper says unmarked taxa are native; otherwise empty. Reference region in notes if stated. Use only the paper, never background knowledge.

definition: Plant family.
rule: As printed, in lower case ('MYRTACEAE' or 'Myrtaceae' -> 'myrtaceae'). Empty if not stated.

allowed_values: obligate | resprouter | O/r | R/o | O/R | code as printed
definition: Resprouting after full canopy scorch: proportion of individuals surviving and resprouting. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Fill only when the paper states the response explicitly: a code with its printed definition, a table column of fire response, or a sentence saying the taxon was killed, resprouted or survived fire. Response only implied (see fire_response_implied) -> leave empty. Map the paper's code by the paper's own definition, using VALUE_MAP: killed / fire-sensitive / obligate seeder -> obligate; resprouting (incl. facultative, e.g. FRR) -> resprouter; mostly killed, some resprout -> O/r; mostly resprout, some killed -> R/o; similar proportions -> O/R. Probable or possible codes (e.g. pK, ?K, ?fs, pR, ?R) -> the main class (obligate or resprouter); notes give the printed code, its definition and the certainty the paper states (e.g. 'probably' = 80-90% sure, 'possibly' = 50-70% sure, as defined by Kubiak 2009); if the paper states no certainty, say 'certainty not stated'. Defined code that fits none of these classes clearly, or 2 or more codes for one taxon at one site and fire -> leave the cell empty; give each printed code and its definition in notes. Never guess a class. Code not defined in the paper -> copy exactly as printed, keeping its case and any '?'; remove spaces next to '?', '/', ';', ',' or brackets ('? r' -> '?r'); keep a space between 2 separate codes ('R s').

allowed_values: obligate | resprouter | O/r | R/o | O/R | code as printed
definition: Fire response (same classes as fire_response_categorical_surv1) that the paper implies but does not state explicitly.
rule: Fill only when fire_response_categorical_surv1 is empty and the paper gives evidence for one class without stating it: e.g. only seedlings recorded after fire, no resprouts; resprouting reported for the population but not this taxon; a trait such as 'lacks lignotuber'; the paper's own assumption ('assumed to be obligate seeder'). Same classes and VALUE_MAP as fire_response_categorical_surv1. Notes: 'fire response implied: <evidence as printed>, p. N'. Never from background knowledge or other papers; no evidence in the paper -> empty.

definition: Resprouting mode.
rule: Map the paper's term with VALUE_MAP (e.g. 'tuberoid' -> 'tuber'; 'basal bud' -> 'basal'); other terms as printed, in lower case and singular ('rhizomes' -> 'rhizome'). Several types joined by '; ', also when printed with 'and', 'or' or 'and/or' ('epicormic and/or basal' -> 'epicormic; basal').

definition: Primary juvenile period: time for plants regenerating from seed after fire to flower.
rule: Fill only when the paper reports the primary juvenile period in months. Then also fill time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4 (months / 12).

definition: Primary juvenile period: time for plants regenerating from seed after fire to flower.
rule: Fill only when the paper reports the primary juvenile period in years.

definition: Age at first flower production from seed. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Time or age to first flowering from seed, when the paper uses other wording than 'primary juvenile period'.

definition: Secondary juvenile period: time for resprouting plants to flower after fire.
rule: Fill only when the paper's term is 'secondary juvenile period'. Unit in time_unit.

definition: Time to first postfire reproduction of resprouting taxa. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Time to first flowering or reproduction of resprouts, when the paper uses other wording than 'secondary juvenile period'.

definition: Maturation age: years for 50% of an even-aged cohort to produce their first viable seed. Trait code from Ferrer-Paris et al. 2025 Fire Ecology Database.
rule: Fill only for maturation age measured as 50% of a cohort producing viable seed, or from pjp_mths (months / 12, no notes entry). Time for 50% of individuals to flower goes to time_to_50_percent_flowering.

definition: Time after fire until 50% of individuals flower.
rule: As stated in the paper, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity, primary juvenile period). Not maturation age. Unit in time_unit.

definition: Time after fire until 80% of individuals flower.
rule: Time after fire until 80% of individuals flower, whatever the paper calls it (e.g. maturity). Unit in time_unit.

definition: Time from fire until recovery, as defined in the paper.
rule: Recovery measure in notes, e.g. 'pre-fire cover'. Unit in time_unit.

definition: Unit of secondary_juvenile_period, time_to_50_percent_flowering, time_to_80_percent_flowering and recovery_time.
rule: Paper's unit. Empty if none of those 4 columns is filled. Mixed units in one row: unit of most values; exceptions in notes.

definition: The time column whose value the error_value belongs to.
rule: Fill only with error_value. Name exactly as in the header, e.g. time_to_50_percent_flowering. 2 or more time values on one row with an error: the value from the paper's main results goes here; the others in notes ('<column> se 0.4').

allowed_values: se | sd | ci95 | ci<N> | ± not defined | as printed
definition: Kind of error the paper prints for the value: standard error, standard deviation, or N% confidence interval.
rule: From the paper's definition (table footnote, methods, figure legend). Bare '±' with no definition: '± not defined'. Other kinds (e.g. credible interval, interquartile range): as printed, lower case. Never infer the kind from the value.

unit: same unit as the value in error_column
definition: Error of the value in error_column, as printed in the paper.
rule: Copy only errors printed in the paper; never compute one (e.g. never SE from SD and n). se or sd: one number. Interval: lower-upper, no spaces. Decimals as printed. Value converted to the column's unit: convert the error the same way and say so in notes. Error only in a figure: empty; note 'error shown in figure only'.

definition: Number of individuals, plants or plots behind the time value, as printed.
rule: The n the paper gives for that species, site and fire (table column, text, figure legend). Whole number. Only a study-wide n (not per species): empty; n in notes. What was counted (plants, plots, quadrats) in notes if stated.

definition: Study site name.
rule: Fill on every row whose values come from a site the paper names or codes, with or without coordinates. Use the site's full name as first defined in the paper's methods or study-site section, also where tables use a code or short form (code 'LCR' defined as 'Lane Cove River valley' -> 'lane cove river valley' on every row of that site); do not add words (e.g. park or region name) or remove words. Map table codes (e.g. column 'A') to that name. Same site = same string on every row of the paper. Shared row for several sites: site names joined by '; '. Sites nested within larger sites (e.g. subsites E1 and E2 within site E): use the finest level at which the paper gives species data; a subsite named only by a code gets that code as printed (e.g. 'E1'). Empty only when the paper names no site for the row's values (e.g. literature values, whole-region summaries); then say why in notes.

definition: latitude of the study area, WGS84.
rule: South negative. 33° 45' S -> -33.75. At most 4 decimals; no trailing zeros ('151.0' -> '151'; '-33.50' -> '-33.5').

definition: longitude of the study area, WGS84.
rule: East positive. 151° 05' E -> 151.0833. At most 4 decimals; no trailing zeros ('151.0' -> '151'; '-33.50' -> '-33.5').

definition: Rainfall of the study location.
rule: Mean annual if stated. Post-fire period -> rainfall_post_fire_mm. Other period -> period in notes.

definition: Rainfall at the study location over a stated period after the fire.
rule: Total over the period in rainfall_post_fire_period, as printed (number or min-max). Mean annual rainfall goes in rainfall_mm, never here. Several post-fire periods: the one closest to the flowering measure (e.g. first year after fire for first flowering in year 1); others in notes. Values per site or per fire on their own rows. Comparison with average (e.g. '40% below average') in notes only. From the paper only; never from a weather source.

definition: Period after the fire that rainfall_post_fire_mm covers.
rule: Fill only with rainfall_post_fire_mm. Lower case, from the fire: 'first 12 months', 'first 2 years', 'winter after fire', or the paper's dates ('jan 1994-dec 1995').

allowed_values: wildfire | prescribed burn | experimental burn | as printed
definition: Type of fire.
rule: Use the listed values; other types as printed.

definition: Season of the fire.
rule: Several seasons joined by '; ' in calendar order summer; autumn; winter; spring (e.g. 'autumn; spring', never 'spring; autumn'). Only a date given -> derive the season and say so in notes.

allowed_values: low | low-moderate | moderate | moderate-high | high | extreme | as printed
definition: Fire severity.
rule: Map the paper's term with VALUE_MAP (e.g. 'very high intensity' or 'severe' -> high); printed term in notes when it differs. Term not in VALUE_MAP (e.g. hot, patchy): as printed.

definition: Where in the paper the row's values are printed: table, figure, appendix or text, with page.
rule: Items '<place>, p. N', joined by '; ', in column order. Place: 'table N', 'fig. N', 'appendix N', 'text', 'methods', 'abstract' (lower case; numbering as printed, e.g. 'table 2a'). Values from different places: name the column before its place where the row has more than one, e.g. 'table 3, p. 8; fire response: table 1, p. 4; site: methods, p. 3'. Page as printed on the paper's pages (journal pagination), written 'p. 342'; range 'pp. 342-343' not used: list each page, 'table 2, p. 342; table 2, p. 343'. Only if no page number is printed: PDF page, 'pdf p. 25'. Supplementary material is never a place here (see supplementary_material). Every row except the NA row.
example: table 2, p. 342 | table 3, p. 8; fire response: table 1, p. 4

definition: Supplementary or supporting material the paper refers to (not available to the pipeline), with its content as the paper describes it.
rule: Each item the paper refers to (e.g. 'Table S1', 'Appendix S2', 'Online Resource 1', 'supporting information'): '<item> (<content as the paper describes it>)', lower case; content not described: '(content not stated)'. Items joined by '; ', in order of first mention. Same string on every row of the paper, NA row included. Empty if the paper refers to none.
example: table s1 (site coordinates, sample sizes); table s2 (plant height data) | supporting information (content not stated)

definition: Assumptions, ambiguities, near-matches, definitions.
rule: Location of the row's values goes in data_location, not here. Items separated by '; ', in this order: (1) notes on this row, each naming its column where it has one, e.g. 'time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a converted from 43 weeks'; (2) paper-wide notes that apply to the row (definition of the code used, site, fire), written as the same text on every row of that paper, with no label such as 'Paper-wide:'. Page numbers as printed on the paper's pages (journal pagination), written 'p. 342'; only if no page number is printed: PDF page, written 'pdf p. 25'.
example: fire_season_categorical derived from fire date 12 january 1994; code 'R' = majority of adult plants resprouted (p. 145)

definition: Full citation of the paper.
rule: APA style, in lower case (author names and title words too). End with the DOI as 'https://doi.org/...' if a DOI is printed in the paper; otherwise no DOI or URL. Same string on every row of that paper. No author, title or year printed in the document: file_name instead; nothing else.
example: benson, d. h. (1985). maturation periods for fire-sensitive shrub species in hawkesbury sandstone vegetation. cunninghamia, 1(3), 339-349.

definition: File stem of the paper the row was extracted from; links rows to the LOG.
rule: Same on every row of that paper.
